record.final_answer:
No. I couldn't find any published number for Marrowlog over TLS, so there's nothing published that shows 50k lines/s will hold.

**What exists:** The only published figure is the maintainers' own Marrowlog 2.4 report from 2026 Q2 (https://marrowlog.example/perf/2026-q2, published 2026-06-18). I fetched it again today and it says the same as the note I had saved. One agent shipped **180,000 lines/s on 1 vCPU / 2 GiB at 85% CPU**, taking the median of three 30-minute runs. The test conditions were:
- plain TCP to the collector; "TLS was not enabled in any run"
- every line 200 bytes or shorter
- disk buffer off, `batch_lines: 500`

The report says TLS, lines over 200 bytes and the disk buffer were **not measured**. It promises TLS numbers in a Q4 report. I guessed that report's address (`/perf/2026-q4`) and got a 404, so it doesn't seem to be out yet. I didn't search the site any further than that.

**Why it doesn't cover your setup:** According to `README.md` and `config/agent.yaml`, your agents run on 1 vCPU with `batch_lines: 500` and the disk buffer off, which matches the test. But your lines average about **900 bytes**, and you'd be adding TLS. Both of those fall outside what was tested.

My own rough arithmetic, not anything the report says: 180k lines × at most 200 bytes is at most about 36 MB/s. 50k lines × 900 bytes is about 45 MB/s. So even without TLS, your load in bytes per second is above anything the test covered. The large line count doesn't carry over to your traffic.

**Suggestion:** Don't plan around the vendor number. Run your own test on a 1-vCPU agent with your real ~900-byte JSON lines and `tls: true` to the collector, and watch CPU at 50k lines/s. Or wait for the Q4 report, though even that will probably use short lines.
